subject: Data residency, TTL for logs, and confirm: we do not train on customer content
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita@fintechinc.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechinc.com, security@fintechinc.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & deletion TTL — assurance on training usage

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for taking this. Procurement and InfoSec at FinTech Inc. have a couple of hard asks as we move the contract toward signature:

1) Explicit contractual language we can present that Redwood will not use customer content to train models or otherwise improve model weights (ever) unless we explicitly opt in.
2) Clarify retention TTLs for all classes of data (request payloads, response tokens, access logs, backups/snapshots) and what is included in the deletion flow triggered by a customer DSR.
3) Residency: we need EU-only processing for request handling and logs; does that require Private deployment or can Dedicated/Hosted support our requirement?

Can you also provide a sample of access log formatting (schema) and the SLA excerpt about retention? Procurement will want these appended to the SOW.

Appreciate a clear single-paragraph statement we can copy into the procurement packet.

Best,
Anita
Anita Shah
Head of Security Operations, FinTech Inc.

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion TTL — assurance on training usage

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front you can copy into procurement: 

"Redwood Inference will not use customer content, logs, or backups to train, evaluate, or improve any machine learning models unless the customer provides explicit written opt-in. All customer content is processed only for the purpose of fulfilling the service and for the limited operational uses described below."

Below are the key retention/residency points and what triggers deletion: 
- Request/response payloads: by default hosted requests are retained for up to 30 days for debugging and billing; EU-only customers can elect a 7- or 30-day retention window in the contract.
- Access logs (authentication, request metadata): default 90 days; can be reduced to 30 days for enterprise EU deployments. A sample log schema is attached.
- KV/ephemeral caches (in-memory tokens, prefix cache): not persisted to durable storage for hosted requests; they are ephemeral per-instance and flushed regularly.
- Backups / snapshots: periodic snapshots are retained for 180 days by default; we can exclude a customer's workspace from snapshot backup on request or provide a separate retention TTL in the SOW.
- Deletion/DSR flow: when a deletion request is received we remove live copies within 48 hours, purge associated logs within the elected retention TTL, and mark any snapshots for expedited tombstoning in the next retention cycle — complete removal from backups can take up to the snapshot TTL unless a contract-level exception is agreed.

I'll attach the SLA excerpt and a small sample of the access log schema. Two quick Qs:
1) Do you need contract language that mandates EU-only physical nodes for all processing (i.e., Private deployment), or is a Hosted EU-region commitment with contractual residency clauses sufficient?
2) Any specific regulatory clause (e.g., PSD2 audit requirement) that would change our standard retention options?

If helpful, Ben can add the procurement-friendly clause and Neha can confirm operational runbooks for expedited snapshot tombstoning.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_DSR_flow.pdf, access_log_sample.csv

From: Anita Shah <anita@fintechinc.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechinc.com, security@fintechinc.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion TTL — assurance on training usage

Thanks, Olga — that language is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security:

- We need the explicit one-line guarantee to appear in the SOW: can you provide the preferred legal wording? Procurement prefers the phrase "will not use customer content to train, tune, or improve models for any purpose."
- Backups: the requirement from our auditors is that customer data must not persist in any long-term backup outside EU. If hosted snapshots are stored encrypted in EU but replicated to another region for DR, that is a blocker for us. Can you confirm whether hosted snapshots are replicated outside the region by default and if replication is configurable per account?
- Evidence: SOC2 log access controls + a copy of a sample access log with pseudonymized entries would be helpful for our audit team.

Thanks,
Anita

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion TTL — assurance on training usage

Hi Anita — following up with specifics you can give to Procurement and to your auditors. Quoting your ask for a one-line legal statement, our standard procurement-approved clause is below; legal can provide a signed addendum if you need it in contract language form: 

"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data to train, tune, or improve any machine learning models, models' weights, or training datasets unless Customer provides explicit prior written consent. For clarity, Customer Data includes request/response payloads, logs, backups, and derived telemetry."

On backups/replication: Hosted EU-region accounts are stored on EU physical nodes and encrypted-at-rest. Snapshots are not replicated to non-EU regions by default for customers who elect EU-only residency in the onboarding form. For Dedicated customers we provide region-pinned GPU pools and avoid cross-region replication. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) remove Redwood-managed replication entirely. If your auditors require written confirmation that no cross-region copies exist, we can add a contractual clause and provide an account-level replication report during onboarding.

Retention table (summary you can copy into an appendix):
- Live request/response payloads: default 30d (options 7d / 30d), deletion within 48h of DSR trigger for live copies.
- Access logs (auth/request metadata): default 90d; enterprise EU option 30d (configurable).
- Ephemeral caches / KV: not durably persisted for hosted ephemeral requests.
- Snapshots/backups: default 180d; can be opted out or TTL shortened via SOW. Complete removal from previous snapshots may take up to the snapshot cycle unless an expedited tombstone is agreed.

Evidence and attachments: attached a pseudonymized access_log_sample.csv and logging_schema.csv; SOC2 report and a short control mapping can be provided under NDA / audit process.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement: include the one-line clause above in the SOW and indicate the retention TTL you prefer (7/30/90/180 options).
2) Security: we can schedule a short call to walk through replication architecture and the snapshot tombstoning runbook.
3) Legal: if you want a signed addendum stating no-training, we can route to our legal team (I can attach a draft).

If helpful, here's a copy-paste friendly paragraph for your packet: 

"Redwood Inference explicitly commits that Customer Data will not be used to train or improve Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent. Hosted EU-region accounts can be configured to limit data persistence to EU physical nodes; backups and snapshots can be excluded from cross-region replication by contract. Deletion requests remove live data within 48 hours and follow the elected retention policy for logs and backups; expedited removal from snapshots is available by agreement."

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachments: logging_schema.csv
